title: Security Deposits Rule on Tempering a Seasonal Peak in the Reconnection Basis Bill
content:
For the Residential Credit Reestablishment Deposit assessed under Security Deposits at the reconnection of a Schedule R or Schedule FH account whose waived deposit was reinstated, a seasonal peak in the account's Electric Service by Rate Schedule bills is tempered before it becomes the reconnection basis bill.

## Rule

A seasonal peak is tempered before it becomes the reconnection basis bill. When the highest monthly bill exceeds the twelve-period average bill by more than the high spike ratio of **2.0** — that is, when it is more than 2.0 times the average — the basis bill is the midpoint of the highest bill and the average bill. When it is more than **1.5** times the average but not more than 2.0 times it, the basis bill is two thirds of the highest bill plus one third of the average bill. Otherwise the peak is not tempered.

## Quantities compared

- **Monthly bills:** a billing period's bill is the sum of that period's usage lines; the twelve monthly bills are those billed in each of the twelve whole months before today, each month read by itself.
- **Highest monthly bill:** the largest of those twelve.
- **Twelve-period average bill:** all usage lines billed in the twelve whole months before today, added together and divided by the number of facility charge lines billed in that time.

## Bands (hypothetical average bill of $150.00)

| Highest monthly bill | Ratio to the average | Reconnection basis bill |
|---|---|---|
| $320.00 | 2.13 | $235.00, the midpoint |
| $300.00 | exactly 2.0 | $250.00, two thirds of $300.00 plus one third of $150.00 |
| $240.00 | 1.6 | $210.00, two thirds of $240.00 plus one third of $150.00 |
| $225.00 | exactly 1.5 | not tempered |

At exactly 2.0 times the average the high ratio is not exceeded; at exactly 1.5 times, the mid ratio is not exceeded.
